items.verification: Implemented as a blocking top-level await (dynamic-import the resolved locale only, prefetch the other on idle) to avoid a flash of untranslated content. Real e2e measurement showed a genuine regression instead: splitting locale JSON into its own chunk turns one bundle fetch into a serial waterfall (main bundle parses -> discovers the dynamic import -> fetches the locale chunk), measurably delaying first render. Broke 5 portfolio e2e tests that interact immediately after page.goto() (keyboard-nav, focus-ring, scroll-restoration, and 2 axe scans -- one caught page-has-heading-one because the page genuinely hadn't rendered yet). Reverted to the original synchronous both-locales-eager version; confirmed the revert restored the clean 85/85 e2e baseline. Not re-attempted differently in this pass -- the original finding's own estimated gain was already flagged as uncertain, and a real regression is worse than the modest bytes saved.

items.verification: Self-hosted via @fontsource/* (Hanken Grotesk, Inter, JetBrains Mono, both apps; Material Symbols Outlined, blog only), replacing the Google Fonts <link> with local @font-face imports in each app's index.css. Did not, on its own, fix the CLS regression found during this wave (see PERF-006) -- that turned out to be a separate, unrelated cause -- but is a legitimate independent improvement (same-origin font files, no fonts.googleapis.com/fonts.gstatic.com round trip), shipped regardless.

items.title: Suspense fallback={null} on every lazy route causes a real CLS regression (0.26, "poor") once the real Lighthouse tooling started working
items.note: Not in the original audit -- Lighthouse's CWV audits were broken (tslib_1.__spreadArray tooling bug, see facts.json) until this wave, so this was unmeasurable before. Root cause, confirmed with a real PerformanceObserver layout-shift trace: every lazy-loaded route (About/Resume/Projects/Contact in portfolio; Post/NotFound in blog) rendered `null` while its chunk fetched, so <main> sat empty and the page briefly settled at exactly viewport height with the footer visible at the bottom; once the chunk resolved and real content rendered, the page grew far taller, and that footer-visible-then-gone transition registered as a huge layout shift. Two wrong hypotheses were tried and measured first (About.tsx's image aspect-ratio; PERF-004's font self-hosting) before the real cause was found via direct trace instrumentation, not guessing. Fix: fallback={<div className="min-h-[150vh]" />} instead of null, both apps. Verified via real Lighthouse: CLS 0.258-0.261 -> 0.000-0.004 on all 4 affected portfolio routes, performance score +10 to +15 points; blog's equivalent routes (already using the same fixed pattern from the start) measured 0.97-0.98 perf / near-zero CLS.
items.verification: Lighthouse (startServerCommand mode, real routes): portfolio / .94 CLS .013, /about .90 CLS .004, /contact .93 CLS .002, /projects .93 CLS .001, /resume .93 CLS 0. Blog /blog .98 CLS 0, /blog/hello-world .97 CLS .002, /adr .98 CLS .001.
